headerDisplay: Enter your DVR/NVR's IP address and login. Cameras are found automatically, and encrypted HiLook / Hik-Connect streams are decrypted for you.

verificationCode.title: Verification code (optional)
verificationCode.description: Only needed if your streams are encrypted and the plugin can't read the code from the device. It's the 6-letter code on the DVR's sticker, or the one you set in Hik-Connect / HiLook.

cameras.title: Cameras (optional)
cameras.description: Rename or hide individual cameras. Leave empty to add every camera the DVR reports.

motion.title: Motion sensors
motion.description: Adds a motion sensor to each camera, driven by the DVR's own motion detection. The DVR must have "Notify Surveillance Center" ticked for motion (Configuration → Event → Motion → Linkage Method); the log says if it doesn't.

motionTimeout.title: Motion reset (seconds)
motionTimeout.description: How long motion stays on after the DVR's last motion event.

oneOf.title: No transcoding (lowest CPU, may look stretched)

subStreamMaxWidth.title: Use sub stream for views up to this width
subStreamMaxWidth.description: 0 = always use the main stream (best quality). E.g. 320 sends Apple Watch views from the DVR's low-resolution sub stream to save CPU.

minBitrate.title: Minimum bitrate (kbps)
minBitrate.description: iOS often requests only ~300 kbps. By default the plugin uses at least 1200 kbps for 720p+ and 600 kbps for smaller views. Set 0 to use exactly what iOS asks for (better on slow remote connections).

webConsole.title: Web console
webConsole.description: Serves the DVR's own web page through Homebridge with live view, playback and motion areas working, at http://<homebridge-ip>:<port>. It is plain HTTP and not password-protected by Homebridge, so don't expose it to the internet.

webConsoleAutoLogin.title: Web console: log in automatically
webConsoleAutoLogin.description: Anyone on your home network who opens the web console is logged in to the DVR as this plugin's account, with no password prompt. The browser receives the password too (the DVR's own login page also keeps it in the tab's session storage). Only turn this on for a trusted network.
